title: Cross-language regression suite
purpose: Pin the committed fixtures' decode, recorded and recomputed digests, canonical digested bytes, required members, DecodeLimits defaults, closed decode-code vocabulary, and SHA-256 known answers, and prove the Python compiler/validator and the C++ decoder agree on the fixtures' canonical body and digest.
inputs: committed T017 fixtures (read-only); golden literals captured from the accepted artifacts
outputs: golden equality assertions and decode-code vocabulary
state: static-immutable test source; decoded value plan-scoped
errors: assertion failure on any golden mismatch
invariants: a golden is never updated to match a drifted artifact

unit_cases.stimulus: decode and compare every pinned field/count
unit_cases.expected: accepted with the pinned plan_version, status, and field-count goldens (T20-REG-01)
accepted with status==inspectable and the pinned unresolved member (T20-REG-02)

unit_cases.precondition: the recorded digest of each fixture
unit_cases.expected: recorded and recomputed digests equal kFixture*Digest (T20-REG-03)

unit_cases.precondition: a digest with and without the domain separator
unit_cases.expected: with separator matches; without/over non-canonical rejected XCOM-DECODE-DIGEST (T20-REG-05)
equal kFixture*FileSha256; anchored T017 fixtures not mutated (T20-REG-07)

unit_cases.precondition: a representative defect per decode code
unit_cases.expected: exactly the nine declared codes; BOUND/UNKNOWN failed, rest rejected (T20-REG-10)

static_checks.rule: cppcheck --error-exitcode=1 --quiet --std=c++20 --language=c++ --suppress=invalidLifetime src/xverse/xcom/src/activation_plan.cpp reports no error/portability defect in the consumed T019 decoder source built into the T020 suites

static_checks.tool: GNU g++ 11.4.0 via CMake target xverse_xcom_activation_plan_t020_<kind>_tests with xverse_xcom_apply_warnings
static_checks.rule: the T020 test target compiles under the project strict warning flags with no warning and no error

note: The Python fixture-digest case is executed by the trusted validation (pytest) measure and is not CTest-discovered.
